dimensions.assessment: Affects international personnel associated with the International Criminal Court, foreign entities assisting the court, U.S. and allied officials, and immediate family members of sanctioned individuals.
dimensions.evidence: The President shall impose... sanctions... with respect to any foreign person the President determines... has directly engaged in or otherwise aided any effort by the International Criminal Court

dimensions.assessment: Imposes severe legal and economic penalties including property blocking, visa revocations, and complete rescission of funds for an international judicial body.
dimensions.evidence: block and prohibit all transactions in all property and interests in property... visa or other entry documentation... shall be revoked

dimensions.assessment: Rescinds all currently appropriated funds for the International Criminal Court and bars future use of appropriated funds for the court.
dimensions.evidence: any amounts appropriated for the International Criminal Court and available for obligation as of such date of enactment are hereby rescinded.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes broad presidential sanction authorities under IEEPA, immigration restrictions, funding rescissions, and reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The President shall exercise all of the powers granted by the International Emergency Economic Powers Act

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory prohibition on funding and ongoing sanction authorities until specific conditions regarding the ICC are met.
dimensions.evidence: On and after the date of the enactment of this Act, no appropriated funds may be used for the International Criminal Court.

missing_information: Exact monetary values of the funds being rescinded from the International Criminal Court.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill imposes mandatory visa- and property-blocking sanctions on foreign persons assisting the International Criminal Court in actions against protected U.S. or allied individuals, rescinds existing ICC funds, and bans future appropriations.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act requires the President to impose financial and visa-related sanctions on foreign individuals and entities that assist the International Criminal Court (ICC) in investigating, arresting, detaining, or prosecuting protected persons, such as U.S. citizens and citizens of certain U.S. allies who are not parties to the ICC's founding treaty. Additionally, the bill rescinds existing funds appropriated for the ICC and bans the use of future appropriated funds for the organization.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to property-blocking and visa-blocking sanctions if they investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute protected U.S. or allied individuals.
Subject to mandatory visa-blocking sanctions and revocation of current visas.
affected_groups.group: Immediate family members of sanctioned foreign persons

affected_groups.effect: Protected from ICC investigation, arrest, detention, or prosecution through U.S. sanctions imposed on those assisting such actions.

key_provisions: Requires the President to impose property-blocking and visa-blocking sanctions on foreign persons who assist, support, or are controlled by those assisting ICC actions against protected persons.
Applies mandatory visa-blocking sanctions to the immediate family members of any foreign person sanctioned under the bill.

Defines 'protected persons' to include U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and people in the U.S., as well as citizens and lawful residents of U.S. allies that are not state parties to the Rome Statute.
Provides a presidential waiver of sanctions in cases determined to be vital to U.S. national security, subject to detailed congressional reporting.
Rescinds all currently appropriated funds for the ICC and prohibits the future use of appropriated funds for the ICC.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts of currently appropriated funds being rescinded for the International Criminal Court are not mentioned in the source.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act requires the President to impose financial and visa-related sanctions on foreign individuals and entities that assist the International Criminal Court (ICC) in investigating, arresting, detaining, or prosecuting protected persons, such as U.S. citizens and citizens of certain U.S. allies who are not parties to the ICC's founding treaty. Additionally, the bill rescinds existing funds appropriated for the ICC and bans the use of future appropriated funds for the organization.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes mandatory economic and travel penalties targeting individuals supporting the International Criminal Court's investigations involving U.S. or allied personnel, and cuts off U.S. financial support for the ICC. The impact score reflects substantial changes to foreign policy enforcement and funding restrictions regarding international tribunals.
